name: Hope Lodge

dates.altered: The 1930s survey sheet: 'In original condition, except for hood over front door and rear part of kitchen wing, which are later additions.'
dates.note: Two dates are on the record because two sources give them: the 1930s HABS sheet prints 'Date of Erection: 1721 - 23' and 'Built in 1721-23 by Samuel Morris'; the Wikipedia infobox prints 1750 with 'Edmund Woolley' as architect. Recorded as the survey states it, with the modern dating noted rather than resolved; the exemplar's year is null for the same reason.

quotes.text: The doors and windows are similar to other houses of the same period, having heavy mouldings, and being higher and narrower than those of a later period.

A hall of unusual width runs the full depth of the house, and o_jens into spacious chambers on both sides. The chief rooms have round-arched doorways, flanked by pilasters with curiously designed caps. The stairway ascends laterally from the rear hall. Throughout the house the woodwork is heavy and substantial and many of the materials are said to have been brought from England.
Back of the house and connected by a brick paved porch(with glass enclosure of later date) are the kitchen and servants' quarters.

Throughout the :,£ain rooms of the first floor there is panelled wainscoting stopping at a chair rail with plastered walls and wood cornices above. In the 'lain first floor rooms the fireplace side is panelled to the ceiling, the shaped 'fireplace facings being of Pennsylvania Blue • marble. Floors of wide random width boards. As no heating, system has ever oeen installed in the Main roo:;is, the woodwork is in perfect original condition.
